#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Scrape a web page and report its key structural properties.

set -uo pipefail

fetch_page() {
    curl -sL --max-time 20 -A "Mozilla/5.0 (scrape.sh)" "$1"
}

response_time_ms() {
    local seconds
    seconds=$(curl -sL -o /dev/null --max-time 20 -w '%{time_total}' "$1")
    awk -v s="${seconds:-0}" 'BEGIN { printf "%.0f", s * 1000 }'
}

extract_domain() {
    local host
    host=$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed -E 's#^[a-zA-Z]+://##; s#/.*$##; s#:[0-9]+$##; s#^[^@]*@##')
    printf '%s' "${host#www.}"
}

page_title() {
    local title
    title=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<<"$1" | grep -oiP '<title[^>]*>.*?</title>' | head -1)
    title=$(sed -E 's#<[^>]*>##g' <<<"$title")
    printf '%s' "$(sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$//g' <<<"$title")"
}

meta_description() {
    local tag
    tag=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<<"$1" | grep -oiP '<meta[^>]+name=["'\'']description["'\''][^>]*>' | head -1)
    printf '%s' "$(grep -oiP 'content=["'\''][^"'\'']*' <<<"$tag" | cut -d'"' -f2- | cut -d"'" -f2-)"
}

count_tags() {
    tr '\n' ' ' <<<"$2" | grep -oiP "<$1[[:space:]>]" | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

body_word_count() {
    local text
    text=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<<"$1" | sed -E 's#<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\1>##gI; s#<[^>]*># #g; s#&[a-zA-Z]+;# #g')
    wc -w <<<"$text" | tr -d ' '
}

page_size_kb() {
    local bytes
    bytes=$(printf '%s' "$1" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
    awk -v b="$bytes" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f", b / 1024 }'
}

scrape() {
    local website=$1 html
    html=$(fetch_page "$website")
    if [[ -z $html ]]; then
        echo "Failed to download $website" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local title links images description words domain size elapsed stamp
    title=$(page_title "$html")
    links=$(count_tags a "$html")
    images=$(count_tags img "$html")
    description=$(meta_description "$html")
    words=$(body_word_count "$html")
    domain=$(extract_domain "$website")
    size=$(page_size_kb "$html")
    elapsed=$(response_time_ms "$website")
    stamp=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')

    printf 'The page "%s" on %s was scraped on %s: it contains %s hyperlinks, ' \
        "${title:-(untitled)}" "$domain" "$stamp" "$links"
    printf '%s images and %s words of body text, is described as "%s", ' \
        "$images" "$words" "${description:-(no meta description)}"
    printf 'weighs %s KB and responded in %s ms.\n' "$size" "$elapsed"
}

main() {
    if [[ $# -ne 1 ]]; then
        echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") <url>" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    scrape "$1"
}

main "$@"

text_es: Write a function `evaluate(project)` that accepts a project folder path containing source code files. The logic must calculate the total number of text files, the total line count across all these files, the number of blank lines, and the number of lines containing comments. It must also determine the name of the file with the highest line count, the number of lines in that largest file, the name of the file with the longest single line, and the length of that longest line. Compute and return these metrics as a formatted sentence describing the project complexity. Example input: a web application folder. Example output: a sentence stating the project has ten files with two hundred total lines, twenty blank lines, thirty comment lines, where the main file contains fifty lines and the router file has the longest line of eighty characters.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Project complexity report: counts text files, lines, blanks and comments.

is_text_file() {
    local file=$1
    local kind
    kind=$(file --brief --mime "$file")
    [[ $kind == text/* ]]
}

count_blank_lines() {
    grep -c '^[[:space:]]*$' "$1" || true
}

count_comment_lines() {
    grep -c -E '^[[:space:]]*(#|//|/\*|\*|--|;)' "$1" || true
}

longest_line_length() {
    awk '{ if (length($0) > max) max = length($0) } END { print max + 0 }' "$1"
}

evaluate() {
    local project=$1
    if [[ ! -d $project ]]; then
        echo "evaluate: '$project' is not a directory" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local files=0 total=0 blanks=0 comments=0
    local biggest="none" biggest_lines=0
    local widest="none" widest_length=0
    local file lines blank comment width

    while IFS= read -r file; do
        is_text_file "$file" || continue
        files=$((files + 1))

        lines=$(wc -l < "$file")
        total=$((total + lines))

        blank=$(count_blank_lines "$file")
        blanks=$((blanks + blank))

        comment=$(count_comment_lines "$file")
        comments=$((comments + comment))

        if (( lines > biggest_lines )); then
            biggest_lines=$lines
            biggest=$(realpath --relative-to="$project" "$file")
        fi

        width=$(longest_line_length "$file")
        if (( width > widest_length )); then
            widest_length=$width
            widest=$(realpath --relative-to="$project" "$file")
        fi
    done < <(find "$project" -type f | sort)

    if (( files == 0 )); then
        echo "The project at $project contains no text files to analyse."
        return 0
    fi

    printf 'The project has %d files with %d total lines, %d blank lines, %d comment lines, where %s contains %d lines and %s has the longest line of %d characters.\n' \
        "$files" "$total" "$blanks" "$comments" \
        "$biggest" "$biggest_lines" "$widest" "$widest_length"
}

main() {
    local target=${1:-.}
    evaluate "$target"
}

main "$@"

text_es: Write a function `analyze(logfile)` that accepts the path to a plain text garbage collection log. The logic must extract the total number of garbage collection events, the timestamp of the first event, the timestamp of the last event, and the total duration of all pauses combined. It must also find the longest single pause duration, the line number where this maximum pause occurred, the shortest pause duration, and the average pause duration across all events. Return a list containing these extracted and computed data points. Example input: a text file with fifty log entries. Example output: a list with fifty, morning, noon, five seconds, one second, line twenty, one millisecond, and one hundred milliseconds.
text_nat:
format_ms() {
    awk -v ms="$1" 'BEGIN {
        if (ms >= 1000) printf "%.3fs\n", ms / 1000
        else printf "%.3fms\n", ms
    }'
}

analyze() {
    local logfile="$1"

    if [[ ! -f "$logfile" ]]; then
        echo "analyze: cannot read '$logfile'" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Every pause is normalised to milliseconds and kept with its line number.
    local pauses
    pauses=$(grep -n -o -E '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(ms|s)\b' "$logfile" |
        awk -F: '{
            value = $2
            if (value ~ /ms$/) { sub(/ms$/, "", value) }
            else { sub(/s$/, "", value); value *= 1000 }
            printf "%d %.3f\n", $1, value
        }')

    if [[ -z "$pauses" ]]; then
        echo "analyze: no GC events found in '$logfile'" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local events
    events=$(printf '%s\n' "$pauses" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    local first_ts
    first_ts=$(grep -m1 -o -E '^[0-9T:.-]+' "$logfile")
    local last_ts
    last_ts=$(grep -o -E '^[0-9T:.-]+' "$logfile" | tail -n 1)

    local sorted
    sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "$pauses" | sort -k2,2g)
    local slowest
    slowest=$(printf '%s\n' "$sorted" | tail -n 1)
    local fastest
    fastest=$(printf '%s\n' "$sorted" | head -n 1)
    local total
    total=$(printf '%s\n' "$pauses" | awk '{ sum += $2 } END { printf "%.3f", sum }')
    local avg_pause
    avg_pause=$(awk -v t="$total" -v n="$events" 'BEGIN { printf "%.3f", t / n }')

    local total_fmt max_fmt min_fmt avg_fmt
    total_fmt=$(format_ms "$total")
    max_fmt=$(format_ms "${slowest#* }")
    min_fmt=$(format_ms "${fastest#* }")
    avg_fmt=$(format_ms "$avg_pause")

    printf '%s\n' "$events" "$first_ts" "$last_ts" "$total_fmt" \
        "$max_fmt" "${slowest% *}" "$min_fmt" "$avg_fmt"
}

main() {
    if [[ $# -ne 1 ]]; then
        echo "usage: $(basename "$0") LOGFILE" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    local -a report
    mapfile -t report < <(analyze "$1") || return 1
    if [[ ${#report[@]} -ne 8 ]]; then
        return 1
    fi

    local labels=(events first_timestamp last_timestamp total_pause \
        max_pause max_pause_line min_pause avg_pause)
    local i
    for i in "${!labels[@]}"; do
        printf '%-16s %s\n' "${labels[$i]}:" "${report[$i]}"
    done
}

main "$@"

text_es: Write a function `validate(desktop)` that accepts a directory path containing desktop application shortcut files. The logic must determine the total number of shortcut files present, the number of files that are missing an execution path, and the number of files pointing to missing icon images. It must also find the name of the shortcut most recently modified, its modification date, the name of the oldest shortcut, its creation or modification date, and the total disk space consumed by the shortcut directory. Return a list of these validation metrics. Example input: a folder with user application launchers. Example output: a list containing twenty, zero, two, browser, yesterday, calculator, last year, and forty kilobytes.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Validate .desktop shortcut files in a directory and report metrics.

count_missing_exec() {
    local dir="$1" file missing=0
    for file in "$dir"/*.desktop; do
        [ -f "$file" ] || continue
        local exec_line
        exec_line=$(grep -m1 '^Exec=' "$file" | cut -d= -f2-)
        if [ -z "${exec_line// /}" ]; then
            missing=$((missing + 1))
        fi
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$missing"
}

count_missing_icons() {
    local dir="$1" file broken=0
    for file in "$dir"/*.desktop; do
        [ -f "$file" ] || continue
        local icon
        icon=$(grep -m1 '^Icon=' "$file" | cut -d= -f2-)
        case "$icon" in
            /*)
                [ -f "$icon" ] || broken=$((broken + 1))
                ;;
            ?*)
                local hit
                hit=$(find /usr/share/icons /usr/share/pixmaps -name "$icon.*" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)
                [ -n "$hit" ] || broken=$((broken + 1))
                ;;
        esac
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$broken"
}

extreme_shortcut() {
    # $1 = dir, $2 = "newest" or "oldest"
    local dir="$1" sorted
    sorted=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.desktop' -printf '%T@ %p\n' | sort -n)
    local line
    if [ "$2" = "newest" ]; then
        line=$(printf '%s\n' "$sorted" | tail -n1)
    else
        line=$(printf '%s\n' "$sorted" | head -n1)
    fi
    local path="${line#* }"
    printf '%s\n' "$(basename "$path" .desktop)"
    date -r "$path" '+%Y-%m-%d'
}

validate() {
    local desktop="$1"
    if [ ! -d "$desktop" ]; then
        printf '%s: not a directory\n' "$desktop" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    local total
    total=$(find "$desktop" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.desktop' -printf '.' | wc -c)
    local no_exec broken_icons
    no_exec=$(count_missing_exec "$desktop")
    broken_icons=$(count_missing_icons "$desktop")
    local newest oldest size
    mapfile -t newest < <(extreme_shortcut "$desktop" newest)
    mapfile -t oldest < <(extreme_shortcut "$desktop" oldest)
    size=$(du -sh "$desktop" | cut -f1)
    printf '%s\n' "$total" "$no_exec" "$broken_icons" \
        "${newest[0]}" "${newest[1]}" "${oldest[0]}" "${oldest[1]}" "$size"
}

main() {
    local dir="${1:-$HOME/.local/share/applications}"
    local metrics
    mapfile -t metrics < <(validate "$dir") || return 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Validate .desktop shortcut files in a directory and report metrics.

count_missing_exec() {
    local dir="$1" file missing=0
    for file in "$dir"/*.desktop; do
        [ -f "$file" ] || continue
        local exec_line
        exec_line=`grep -m1 '^Exec=' "$file" | cut -d= -f2-`
        if [ -z "${exec_line// /}" ]; then
            missing=$((missing + 1))
        fi
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$missing"
}

count_missing_icons() {
    local dir="$1" file broken=0
    for file in "$dir"/*.desktop; do
        [ -f "$file" ] || continue
        local icon
        icon=`grep -m1 '^Icon=' "$file" | cut -d= -f2-`
        case "$icon" in
            /*)
                [ -f "$icon" ] || broken=$((broken + 1))
                ;;
            ?*)
                local hit
                hit=`find /usr/share/icons /usr/share/pixmaps -name "$icon.*" -print -quit 2>/dev/null`
                [ -n "$hit" ] || broken=$((broken + 1))
                ;;
        esac
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$broken"
}

extreme_shortcut() {
    # $1 = dir, $2 = "newest" or "oldest"
    local dir="$1" sorted
    sorted=`find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.desktop' -printf '%T@ %p\n' | sort -n`
    local line
    if [ "$2" = "newest" ]; then
        line=`printf '%s\n' "$sorted" | tail -n1`
    else
        line=`printf '%s\n' "$sorted" | head -n1`
    fi
    local path="${line#* }"
    printf '%s\n' "`basename "$path" .desktop`"
    date -r "$path" '+%Y-%m-%d'
}

validate() {
    local desktop="$1"
    if [ ! -d "$desktop" ]; then
        printf '%s: not a directory\n' "$desktop" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    local total
    total=`find "$desktop" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.desktop' -printf '.' | wc -c`
    local no_exec broken_icons
    no_exec=`count_missing_exec "$desktop"`
    broken_icons=`count_missing_icons "$desktop"`
    local newest oldest size
    mapfile -t newest < <(extreme_shortcut "$desktop" newest)
    mapfile -t oldest < <(extreme_shortcut "$desktop" oldest)
    size=`du -sh "$desktop" | cut -f1`
    printf '%s\n' "$total" "$no_exec" "$broken_icons" \
        "${newest[0]}" "${newest[1]}" "${oldest[0]}" "${oldest[1]}" "$size"
}

main() {
    local dir="${1:-$HOME/.local/share/applications}"
    local metrics
    mapfile -t metrics < <(validate "$dir") || return 1
    local labels=(total no_exec broken_icons newest newest_date oldest oldest_date size)
    local i
    for i in "${!labels[@]}"; do
        printf '%-13s %s\n' "${labels[i]}:" "${metrics[i]}"
    done
}

main "$@"

text_es: Write a function `process(transactions)` that accepts a path to a comma separated values file containing retail sales transactions. The logic must determine the total number of transactions, the sum of all transaction amounts, the highest single transaction amount, and the lowest single transaction amount. It must also find the average transaction amount, the total number of unique customer identifiers, the date of the earliest transaction, and the date of the latest transaction. Return a list of these financial metrics. Example input: a file with daily store sales. Example output: a list containing one hundred transactions, five thousand dollars, two hundred dollars, five dollars, fifty dollars, eighty customers, January first, and January thirty first.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CSV columns: date,customer_id,amount

count_transactions() {
    local file="$1"
    tail -n +2 "$file" | grep -c ','
}

sum_amounts() {
    local file="$1"
    tail -n +2 "$file" | awk -F',' '{ s += $3 } END { printf "%.2f", s }'
}

extreme_amount() {
    local file="$1" mode="$2"
    tail -n +2 "$file" | cut -d',' -f3 | sort -g | { [ "$mode" = max ] && tail -n 1 || head -n 1; }
}

unique_customers() {
    local file="$1"
    tail -n +2 "$file" | cut -d',' -f2 | sort -u | grep -c .
}

boundary_date() {
    local file="$1" mode="$2"
    tail -n +2 "$file" | cut -d',' -f1 | sort | { [ "$mode" = latest ] && tail -n 1 || head -n 1; }
}

process() {
    local transactions="$1"
    if [ ! -f "$transactions" ]; then
        echo "process: cannot read '$transactions'" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local total
    total=$(count_transactions "$transactions")
    if [ "$total" -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "process: no transaction rows in '$transactions'" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local sum
    sum=$(sum_amounts "$transactions")
    local highest
    highest=$(extreme_amount "$transactions" max)
    local lowest
    lowest=$(extreme_amount "$transactions" min)
    local average
    average=$(awk -v s="$sum" -v n="$total" 'BEGIN { printf "%.2f", s / n }')
    local customers
    customers=$(unique_customers "$transactions")
    local earliest
    earliest=$(boundary_date "$transactions" earliest)
    local latest
    latest=$(boundary_date "$transactions" latest)

    printf '%s\n' "$total" "$sum" "$highest" "$lowest" "$average" \
        "$customers" "$earliest" "$latest"
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
        echo "usage: $(basename "$0") transactions.csv" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    local metrics
    mapfile -t metrics < <(process "$1") || return 1

    local labels=(transactions total highest lowest average customers earliest latest)
    local i
    for i in "${!metrics[@]}"; do
        printf '%-13s %s\n' "${labels[$i]}:" "${metrics[$i]}"
    done
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
    main "$@"
fi

text_es: Write a function `aggregate(results)` that accepts a path to a text file containing the output of a software test suite. The logic must extract the total number of tests executed, the number of tests that passed successfully, the number of tests that failed, and the number of tests that were skipped. It must also find the name of the test module that took the longest to run, its execution duration, the overall duration of the entire test suite, and the name of the operating system environment where the tests were executed. Return a list containing these extracted values. Example input: a file with automated test results. Example output: a list with fifty, forty, five, five, database tests, ten seconds, one minute, and linux.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Aggregate the summary numbers of a test-suite log file.
#
# Expected log format (one item per line):
#   OS: linux
#   Total: 50
#   Passed: 40
#   Failed: 5
#   Skipped: 5
#   Duration: 60
#   MODULE database_tests 10
#   MODULE api_tests 4

set -uo pipefail

field() {
    local line
    line=$(grep -m1 -E "^[[:space:]]*$2:" "$1")
    [[ -n $line ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${line#*:}" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//'
}

require_field() {
    local value
    value=$(field "$1" "$2") || { printf 'aggregate: missing field "%s"\n' "$2" >&2; return 1; }
    printf '%s\n' "$value"
}

slowest_module() {
    local line
    line=$(awk '$1 == "MODULE" { print $3, $2 }' "$1" | sort -nr | head -n1)
    [[ -n $line ]] || { printf 'aggregate: no MODULE lines found\n' >&2; return 1; }
    printf '%s %s\n' "${line#* }" "${line%% *}"
}

format_duration() {
    local minutes=$(( $1 / 60 )) seconds=$(( $1 % 60 ))
    if (( minutes > 0 )); then
        printf '%d minute(s) %d second(s)\n' "$minutes" "$seconds"
    else
        printf '%d second(s)\n' "$seconds"
    fi
}

aggregate() {
    local results=$1
    [[ -f $results ]] || { printf 'aggregate: %s: no such file\n' "$results" >&2; return 1; }

    local total passed failed skipped os slow raw_total suite slow_time
    total=$(require_field "$results" Total) || return 1
    passed=$(require_field "$results" Passed) || return 1
    failed=$(require_field "$results" Failed) || return 1
    skipped=$(require_field "$results" Skipped) || return 1
    os=$(require_field "$results" OS) || return 1

    if (( passed + failed + skipped != total )); then
        printf 'aggregate: warning: counts do not add up to %s\n' "$total" >&2
    fi

    slow=$(slowest_module "$results") || return 1
    slow_time=$(format_duration "${slow##* }")
    raw_total=$(require_field "$results" Duration) || return 1
    suite=$(format_duration "$raw_total")

    printf '%s\n' "$total" "$passed" "$failed" "$skipped" \
        "${slow%% *}" "$slow_time" "$suite" "$os"
}

report() {
    local labels=(Total Passed Failed Skipped "Slowest module" "Slowest time" "Suite time" OS)
    local i
    for i in "${!labels[@]}"; do
        printf '%-16s %s\n' "${labels[i]}:" "$1"
        shift
    done
}

main() {
    local list values
    list=$(aggregate "${1:-results.txt}") || return 1
    mapfile -t values <<<"$list"
    report "${values[@]}"
}

main "$@"

Create a script that reads a text file line by line and prints each line in reverse order. 

Input: A single filename as a command-line argument.
Output: Each line of the input file, reversed.

Example 1 (content of input.txt: 'hello\nworld'):
$ bash script.sh input.txt
olleh
dlrow

Example 2 (content of empty.txt: ''):
$ bash script.sh empty.txt
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Print each line of a text file with the characters of that line in reverse order.
set -u

usage() {
    local prog
    prog=$(basename "$0")
    printf 'usage: %s FILE\n' "$prog" >&2
}

reverse_string() {
    local s=$1 out="" i
    for (( i = ${#s} - 1; i >= 0; i-- )); do
        out+=${s:i:1}
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$out"
}

count_lines() {
    local count
    count=$(grep -c '' "$1")
    printf '%s\n' "$count"
}

report() {
    local file=$1 name total
    name=$(basename "$file")
    total=$(count_lines "$file")
    printf 'reversed %s line(s) of %s\n' "$total" "$name" >&2
}

process_file() {
    local file=$1 line reversed
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do
        line=${line%$'\r'}
        reversed=$(reverse_string "$line")
        printf '%s\n' "$reversed"
    done < "$file"
}

validate_input() {
    local file=$1
    if [[ -d $file ]]; then
        printf 'error: %s is a directory\n' "$file" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -e $file ]]; then
        printf 'error: %s: no such file\n' "$file" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -r $file ]]; then
        printf 'error: %s: permission denied\n' "$file" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

main() {
    if (( $# != 1 )); then
        usage
        return 2
    fi
    validate_input "$1" || return 1
    process_file "$1"
    report "$1"
}

main "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Create a ".bak" copy of a file in the same directory.

set -u

backup_name() {
    local src="$1"
    printf '%s.bak' "$src"
}

validate_source() {
    local src="$1"
    if [[ ! -e "$src" ]]; then
        printf "Error: File '%s' not found.\n" "$src" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -f "$src" ]]; then
        printf "Error: '%s' is not a regular file.\n" "$src" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -r "$src" ]]; then
        printf "Error: File '%s' is not readable.\n" "$src" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    local dir
    dir="$(dirname -- "$src")"
    if [[ ! -w "$dir" ]]; then
        printf "Error: Directory '%s' is not writable.\n" "$dir" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

make_backup() {
    local src="$1"
    local dest
    dest="$(backup_name "$src")"
    if ! cp -p -- "$src" "$dest"; then
        printf "Error: Could not copy '%s' to '%s'.\n" "$src" "$dest" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s' "$dest"
}

report() {
    local src="$1" dest="$2"
    local size
    size="$(wc -c < "$dest" | tr -d ' ')"
    printf 'Backed up %s -> %s (%s bytes)\n' "$(basename -- "$src")" "$dest" "$size" >&2
}

main() {
    if [[ $# -ne 1 ]]; then
        printf 'Usage: %s FILENAME\n' "$(basename -- "$0")" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    local source="$1"
    validate_source "$source" || return 1

    local backup
    backup="$(make_backup "$source")" || return 1
    report "$source" "$backup"
}

main "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Requires at least one command-line argument and reports whether any
# were supplied.

set -u

readonly EXIT_USAGE=64

program_name() {
    local name
    name=$(basename -- "$0")
    printf '%s\n' "$name"
}

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [--] ARGUMENT [ARGUMENT...]\n' "$(program_name)"
    printf '  -h, --help   show this help text and exit\n'
    printf 'Prints a confirmation when at least one argument is given.\n'
}

hint() {
    printf "Try '%s --help' for more information.\n" "$(program_name)"
}

# Consumes any leading options and writes the number of remaining
# operands to stdout. Returns 1 for an unknown option and 2 when help
# was requested.
parse_options() {
    while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            -h|--help)
                return 2
                ;;
            --)
                shift
                break
                ;;
            -?*)
                printf '%s: unknown option: %s\n' "$(program_name)" "$1" >&2
                return 1
                ;;
            *)
                break
                ;;
        esac
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$#"
}

require_arguments() {
    if [ "$1" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf 'Error: No arguments provided.\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Requires at least one command-line argument and reports whether any
# were supplied.

set -u

readonly EXIT_USAGE=64

program_name() {
    local name
    name=`basename -- "$0"`
    printf '%s\n' "$name"
}

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [--] ARGUMENT [ARGUMENT...]\n' "`program_name`"
    printf '  -h, --help   show this help text and exit\n'
    printf 'Prints a confirmation when at least one argument is given.\n'
}

hint() {
    printf "Try '%s --help' for more information.\n" "`program_name`"
}

# Consumes any leading options and writes the number of remaining
# operands to stdout. Returns 1 for an unknown option and 2 when help
# was requested.
parse_options() {
    while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            -h|--help)
                return 2
                ;;
            --)
                shift
                break
                ;;

                return 1
                ;;
            *)
                break
                ;;

    done
    printf '%s\n' "$#"
}

require_arguments() {
    if [ "$1" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf 'Error: No arguments provided.\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf 'Arguments provided:\n'
}

            ;;

            hint >&2
            return "$EXIT_USAGE"

main "$@"

text_es:
Write a script that takes two integer arguments, START and END. It should use a `for` loop to print all numbers from START to END (inclusive), each on a new line. Assume START <= END.

Input: Two integers, START and END.
Output: Numbers from START to END.

Example 1:
$ bash script.sh 1 3
1
2
3

Example 2:
$ bash script.sh 5 5
5
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# script.sh -- print every integer from START to END, inclusive.
#
# Usage: bash script.sh START END

set -u

PROG=$(basename "$0")
SEQ=$(command -v seq || true)

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s START END\n' "$PROG" >&2
}

# Echo an optionally signed decimal integer without a redundant sign or
# leading zeros; complain and fail if the text is not an integer.
parse_int() {
    local text=$1 sign= digits=$1

    case $text in
        -*) sign=-; digits=${text#-} ;;
        +*) digits=${text#+} ;;
    esac

    case $digits in
        '' | *[!0-9]*)
            printf '%s: not an integer: %s\n' "$PROG" "$text" >&2
            return 1
            ;;
    esac

    printf '%s%d\n' "$sign" "$((10#$digits))"
}

print_range() {
    local n

    for n in $("$SEQ" "$1" "$2"); do
        printf '%s\n' "$n"
    done
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -ne 2 ]; then
        usage
        exit 2
    fi

    local start end
    start=$(parse_int "$1") || exit 2
    end=$(parse_int "$2") || exit 2

    if [ -z "$SEQ" ]; then
        printf '%s: cannot find seq in PATH\n' "$PROG" >&2
        exit 127
    fi

    if [ "$start" -gt "$end" ]; then
        printf '%s: START (%s) must not exceed END (%s)\n' \
            "$PROG" "$start" "$end" >&2
        exit 2
    fi

    print_range "$start" "$end"
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Create a script that takes a directory path as an argument. It should recursively count the total number of regular files in that directory and all its subdirectories. Print the total count.

Input: Directory path.
Output: Total file count.

Example 1 (dir 'root' contains: 'file1', 'subdir1/file2', 'subdir1/subdir2/file3'):
$ bash script.sh root
3

Example 2 (dir 'empty_root' contains: no files):
$ bash script.sh empty_root
0
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Recursively count the regular files in a directory tree and print the total.

set -u

prog=$(basename -- "$0")

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [-L] DIRECTORY\n' "$prog" >&2
}

die() {
    printf '%s: %s\n' "$prog" "$1" >&2
    exit 1
}

# The traversal relies on find, so resolve it once and fail early if missing.
find_bin=$(command -v find) || die 'required command not found: find'

# Drop redundant trailing slashes so the path appears cleanly in messages.
normalize_path() {
    local path=$1

    while [[ $path != / && $path == */ ]]; do
        path=${path%/}
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$path"
}

# Make sure the argument really is a directory that can be walked into.
validate_dir() {
    local dir=$1

    [[ -e $dir ]] || die "no such path: $dir"
    if [[ ! -d $dir ]]; then
        die "not a directory: $(realpath -m -- "$dir" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$dir")"
    fi
    [[ -r $dir && -x $dir ]] || die "permission denied: $dir"
}

# Count the regular files below the directory. Names may contain any character,
# including newlines, so entries are emitted NUL-terminated and it is the NUL
# bytes that get counted. Anything find could not read is reported on stderr.
count_files() {
    local dir=$1
    local errlog nuls

    errlog=$(mktemp)
    nuls=$("$find_bin" "${find_opts[@]}" "$dir" -type f -print0 2>"$errlog" | tr -dc '\0' | wc -c)
    if [[ -s $errlog ]]; then
        sed "s|^|$prog: |" "$errlog" >&2
    fi
    rm -f -- "$errlog"
    printf '%s\n' "$((nuls))"
}

# -H makes find descend into the directory even when the given path is a
# symlink; -L additionally follows symlinks found inside the tree.
find_opts=(-H)

main() {
    while getopts ':L' opt; do
        case $opt in
            L) find_opts=(-L) ;;
            *) usage; exit 1 ;;
        esac
    done
    shift $((OPTIND - 1))

    (( $# == 1 )) || { usage; exit 1; }

    local target total
    target=$(normalize_path "$1")
    validate_dir "$target"

    total=$(count_files "$target")
    printf '%s\n' "$total"
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Create a script that takes a single string as an argument and counts the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) in it. Print the total count.

Input: A single string.
Output: Vowel count.

Example 1:
$ bash script.sh "Hello World"
3

Example 2:
$ bash script.sh "Rhythm"
0
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Count the vowels (a, e, i, o, u - case-insensitive) in a string.
# Usage: bash script.sh "some string"

set -u

# Normalise the input to lower case so a single vowel set suffices.
to_lower() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'
}

# Remove everything that is not a vowel; what is left is one char per vowel.
vowels_only() {
    local lowered
    lowered=$(to_lower "$1")
    printf '%s' "$lowered" | tr -cd 'aeiou'
}

# Total number of vowels in the string.
count_vowels() {
    local kept
    kept=$(vowels_only "$1")
    printf '%s' "${#kept}"
}

# How many times one specific vowel occurs, for the per-vowel breakdown.
count_one_vowel() {
    local kept
    kept=$(vowels_only "$1" | tr -cd "$2")
    printf '%s' "${#kept}"
}

# Human readable breakdown, e.g. "a:0 e:1 i:0 o:2 u:0".
vowel_breakdown() {
    local text=$1 vowel count parts=()
    for vowel in a e i o u; do
        count=$(count_one_vowel "$text" "$vowel")
        parts+=("$vowel:$count")
    done
    printf '%s' "${parts[*]}"
}

usage() {
    local name
    name=$(basename "$0")
    printf 'usage: %s "string"\n' "$name" >&2
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
        usage
        return 1
    fi

    local text=$1 total
    total=$(count_vowels "$text")
    printf '%s\n' "$total"

    if [ -n "${VERBOSE:-}" ]; then
        local breakdown
        breakdown=$(vowel_breakdown "$text")
        printf 'breakdown: %s\n' "$breakdown" >&2
    fi

    return 0
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Write a script that takes a command name (e.g., 'ls', 'python3', 'nonexistent_cmd') as an argument. It should print 'Command exists.' or 'Command does not exist.'.

Input: A command name string.
Output: Command existence status.

Example 1:
$ bash script.sh ls
Command exists.

Example 2:
$ bash script.sh non_existent_command_123
Command does not exist.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Report whether a given command name is available in the current shell.

set -u

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [-v] COMMAND\n' "$(basename "$0")" >&2
}

# Succeeds when the name is a builtin, function, alias, keyword or file in PATH.
command_exists() {
    local name=$1
    command -v -- "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# Absolute path of an executable, following symlinks; empty for non-files.
resolve_target() {
    local name=$1
    local location
    location=$(command -v -- "$name")
    if [[ -x $location ]]; then
        readlink -f -- "$location"
    fi
}

# Extra detail sent to stderr in verbose mode, so stdout stays a single line.
describe_command() {
    local name=$1
    local target
    printf 'name: %s\nkind: %s\n' "$name" "$(type -t -- "$name")" >&2
    target=$(resolve_target "$name")
    if [[ -n $target ]]; then
        printf 'path: %s\nsize: %s bytes\n' "$target" "$(stat -c %s -- "$target")" >&2
    fi
}

main() {
    local verbose=0
    while getopts ':v' opt; do
        case $opt in
            v) verbose=1 ;;
            *) usage; return 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    shift $((OPTIND - 1))

    if [[ $# -ne 1 || -z ${1//[[:space:]]/} ]]; then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local name=$1
    if command_exists "$name"; then
        echo 'Command exists.'
        if [[ $verbose -eq 1 ]]; then
            describe_command "$name"
        fi
        return 0
    fi

    echo 'Command does not exist.'
    if [[ $verbose -eq 1 ]]; then
        printf 'searched PATH:\n%s\n' "$(tr ':' '\n' <<<"$PATH")" >&2
    fi
    return 1
}

main "$@"

Create a script that takes a filename or directory path as an argument. It should print the file's permissions in symbolic (e.g., -rw-r--r--) and octal (e.g., 644) format.

Input: Filename or directory path.
Output: Symbolic and octal permissions.

Example 1 (for a file 'test.txt' with permissions 644):
$ bash script.sh test.txt
Symbolic: -rw-r--r--
Octal: 644

Example 2 (for a directory 'my_dir' with permissions 755):
$ bash script.sh my_dir
Symbolic: drwxr-xr-x
Octal: 755

Write a script that takes a message string as an argument. It should append this message, along with a timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS), to a file named 'app.log'. If 'app.log' doesn't exist, create it.

Input: A message string.
Output: No direct output, but 'app.log' is updated.

Example 1 (app.log empty):
$ bash script.sh "User logged in"
(app.log content: '2023-10-27 11:00:00 User logged in')

Example 2 (app.log has existing entry):
$ bash script.sh "Data processed"
(app.log content: '...\n2023-10-27 11:01:00 Data processed')
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Append a timestamped message to app.log, creating the file when needed.
set -euo pipefail

PROG=$(basename -- "$0")
LOG_FILE="${LOG_FILE:-app.log}"
MAX_ENTRIES="${MAX_ENTRIES:-1000}"

timestamp() {
    date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'
}

# A log entry must stay on a single line, so fold whitespace and trim the tail.
sanitize() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | tr '\n\t' '  ' | sed -e 's/[[:space:]]\{1,\}$//'
}

ensure_log() {
    local file=$1 dir
    dir=$(dirname -- "$file")
    [ -d "$dir" ] || mkdir -p -- "$dir"
    [ -f "$file" ] || : > "$file"
}

entry_count() {
    local file=$1
    if [ -f "$file" ]; then
        wc -l < "$file" | tr -d '[:space:]'
    else
        printf '0'
    fi
}

# Keep app.log from growing without bound: archive it once it is full.
rotate_log() {
    local file=$1 count stamp
    count=$(entry_count "$file")
    if [ "$count" -ge "$MAX_ENTRIES" ]; then
        stamp=$(date '+%Y%m%d%H%M%S')
        mv -- "$file" "$file.$stamp"
        : > "$file"
    fi
}

log_message() {
    local message
    message=$(sanitize "$1")
    if [ -z "$message" ]; then
        return 1
    fi
    ensure_log "$LOG_FILE"
    rotate_log "$LOG_FILE"
    printf '%s %s\n' "$(timestamp)" "$message" >> "$LOG_FILE"
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -lt 1 ]; then
        printf 'usage: %s <message>\n' "$PROG" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    if ! log_message "$*"; then
        printf '%s: refusing to log an empty message\n' "$PROG" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

main "$@"

Input: Directory path.
Output: Total disk usage.

Example 1 (dir 'my_data' has 100MB of files):

100M

Example 2 (dir 'empty_dir' has no files):
$ bash script.sh empty_dir
4.0K (or similar for empty directory metadata)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Print the total disk usage of a directory in human-readable form.
#
# usage: bash script.sh DIRECTORY

set -uo pipefail

die() {
    printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2
    exit 1
}

require_du() {
    command -v du >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "the 'du' utility is not available"
}

# Check the argument really is a usable directory and echo its absolute path.
validate_directory() {
    local path=$1 resolved
    [ -n "$path" ] || die "directory path must not be empty"
    [ -e "$path" ] || die "no such file or directory: $path"
    [ -d "$path" ] || die "not a directory: $path"
    [ -r "$path" ] || die "directory is not readable: $path"
    resolved=$(cd -- "$path" && pwd -P) || die "cannot enter directory: $path"
    printf '%s\n' "$resolved"
}

# Apparent-size-independent usage, in KiB blocks.
usage_kib() {
    local kib
    kib=$(du -sk -- "$1" | awk 'NR==1 {print $1}') || die "du failed on $1"

Input: A directory path.
Output: A string indicating emptiness.

Example 2: `bash script.sh /home/user`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Report whether a directory is empty, including hidden entries.

set -u

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s DIRECTORY\n' "$(basename "$0")" >&2
}

# Resolve the argument to an absolute path so messages are unambiguous.
resolve_path() {
    local target=$1
    local dir base

    dir=$(dirname -- "$target")
    base=$(basename -- "$target")

    if [[ -d $target ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$(cd -- "$target" && pwd -P)"
    elif [[ -d $dir ]]; then
        printf '%s/%s\n' "$(cd -- "$dir" && pwd -P)" "$base"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$target"
    fi
}

validate_directory() {
    local path=$1

    if [[ ! -e $path ]]; then
        printf 'Error: %s does not exist\n' "$path" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -d $path ]]; then
        printf 'Error: %s is not a directory\n' "$path" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -r $path || ! -x $path ]]; then
        printf 'Error: %s is not readable\n' "$path" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

# Count entries other than "." and ".." without relying on glob expansion.
count_entries() {
    local path=$1
    local total

    total=$(find "$path" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -printf 'x\n' | wc -l)
    printf '%s\n' "${total// /}"
}

main() {
    if (( $# != 1 )); then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local path
    path=$(resolve_path "$1")

    validate_directory "$path" || return 1

    if [[ $(count_entries "$path") -eq 0 ]]; then
        printf 'Directory is empty\n'
    else
        printf 'Directory is not empty\n'
    fi
}

main "$@"

Create a script that takes a directory path as an argument. It should recursively count the total number of subdirectories within that path (excluding the initial directory itself).

Input: A directory path.
Output: An integer count.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Recursively count the subdirectories contained in a given directory,
# not counting the directory itself.

set -u

usage() {
    printf 'usage: %s DIRECTORY\n' "$(basename "$0")" >&2
}

# Resolve the argument to an absolute, symlink-free path when possible so
# that the report shows an unambiguous location.
resolve_path() {
    local target=$1
    if resolved=$(readlink -f -- "$target" 2>/dev/null); then
        printf '%s\n' "$resolved"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$target"
    fi
}

validate_dir() {
    local dir=$1
    if [[ ! -e $dir ]]; then
        printf '%s: no such file or directory\n' "$dir" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -d $dir ]]; then
        printf '%s: not a directory\n' "$dir" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -r $dir || ! -x $dir ]]; then
        printf '%s: permission denied\n' "$dir" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

# Print the number of directories strictly below $1.
count_subdirs() {
    local dir=$1
    local found
    found=$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -type d -printf 'd\n' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    printf '%s\n' "$found"
}

# Directories that live immediately under $1, useful for the summary line.
count_immediate_subdirs() {
    local dir=$1
    printf '%s\n' "$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -printf 'd\n' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
}

report() {
    local dir=$1 total=$2
    local direct
    direct=$(count_immediate_subdirs "$dir")
    printf '%s: %d subdirectories (%d at the top level)\n' "$dir" "$total" "$direct" >&2
}

main() {
    if (( $# != 1 )); then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local dir
    dir=$(resolve_path "$1")
    validate_dir "$dir" || return 1

    local total
    total=$(count_subdirs "$dir")
    report "$dir" "$total"
    printf '%d\n' "$total"
}

main "$@"

Write a script that takes a string and a substring to remove as arguments. It should print the original string with all occurrences of the specified substring removed.

Input: A string and a substring.
Output: The modified string.

Example 1: `bash script.sh "banana republic" ana`
Example 2: `bash script.sh "hello world hello" hello`
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Remove every occurrence of a substring from a string.
#
#   script.sh "banana republic" ana   ->  bna republic
#   script.sh "hello world hello" hello

set -u

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s "<string>" "<substring>"\n' "$(basename "$0")" >&2
}

# Delete all occurrences of $2 inside $1 and print the result.
remove_all() {
    printf '%s' "${1//"$2"/}"
}

# How many copies of $2 were present in $1? Derived from the length
# that disappears when the substring is stripped.
count_occurrences() {
    local stripped
    stripped=$(remove_all "$1" "$2")
    printf '%d' $(( (${#1} - ${#stripped}) / ${#2} ))
}

# Make empty values visible in the human readable report.
describe() {
    if [[ -z $1 ]]; then
        printf '(empty)'
    else
        printf '%s' "$1"
    fi
}

# Diagnostic summary, written to stderr so stdout stays a clean result.
report() {
    local original=$1 needle=$2 result
    result=$(remove_all "$original" "$needle")
    printf 'original : %s\n' "$(describe "$original")"
    printf 'remove   : %s\n' "$needle"
    printf 'count    : %s\n' "$(count_occurrences "$original" "$needle")"
    printf 'result   : %s\n' "$(describe "$result")"
}

main() {
    if (( $# != 2 )); then
        printf 'error: expected 2 arguments, got %d\n' "$#" >&2
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local original=$1 needle=$2
    if [[ -z $needle ]]; then
        printf 'error: the substring to remove must not be empty\n' >&2
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    printf '%s\n' "$(remove_all "$original" "$needle")"
    report "$original" "$needle" >&2
}

main "$@"

Develop a script that takes an integer N as an argument. It should generate and print a random password of length N, consisting of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, and digits.

Input: An integer N.
Output: A random string of length N.

Example 1: `bash script.sh 8`
Example 2: `bash script.sh 12`
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Generate a random alphanumeric password of a requested length.

set -u

CHARSET='ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789'

usage() {
    echo "usage: $(basename "$0") N" >&2
    echo "  N: password length (positive integer)" >&2
}

validate_length() {
    local raw="$1"
    local trimmed
    trimmed=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | tr -d '[:space:]')

    case "$trimmed" in
        ''|*[!0-9]*)
            echo "error: '$raw' is not a non-negative integer" >&2
            return 1
            ;;
    esac

    if [ "$trimmed" -lt 1 ]; then
        echo "error: length must be at least 1" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    printf '%s' "$trimmed"
}

random_index() {
    local modulus="$1"
    local value
    value=$(od -An -N2 -tu2 < /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')
    echo $(( value % modulus ))
}

random_char() {
    local pos
    pos=$(random_index "${#CHARSET}")
    printf '%s' "${CHARSET:pos:1}"
}

generate_password() {
    local length="$1"
    local out=''
    local i

    for (( i = 0; i < length; i++ )); do
        out="${out}$(random_char)"
    done

    printf '%s' "$out"
}

describe_password() {
    local password="$1"
    local digits uppers lowers
    digits=$(printf '%s' "$password" | tr -cd '0-9' | wc -c)
    uppers=$(printf '%s' "$password" | tr -cd 'A-Z' | wc -c)
    lowers=$(printf '%s' "$password" | tr -cd 'a-z' | wc -c)

    printf 'length=%d upper=%d lower=%d digits=%d\n' \
        "${#password}" "$uppers" "$lowers" "$digits" >&2
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local length password
    length=$(validate_length "$1") || return 1
    password=$(generate_password "$length")

    echo "$password"
    describe_password "$password"
}

main "$@"

Create a script that takes a file path as an argument. It should print 'Executable' if the file exists and is executable by the current user, otherwise 'Not Executable'.

Input: A file path.
Output: 'Executable' or 'Not Executable'.

Example 1: `bash script.sh /bin/ls`
Example 2: `bash script.sh /etc/hosts`
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Report whether a given path exists and is executable by the current user.

set -u

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s PATH\n' "$(basename -- "$0")" >&2
}

# Resolve the argument to an absolute path so symlinks and relative
# paths are reported unambiguously.
resolve_path() {
    local target=$1
    local dir base
    dir=$(dirname -- "$target")
    base=$(basename -- "$target")
    if [ -d "$dir" ]; then
        printf '%s/%s\n' "$(cd -- "$dir" && pwd -P)" "$base"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$target"
    fi
}

check_executable() {
    if [ -x "$1" ]; then
        printf 'Executable\n'
    else
        printf 'Not Executable\n'
    fi
}

# Human readable detail for stderr: what kind of object it is and how
# its permission bits are set.
describe_path() {
    local target=$1
    local kind mode

    if [ ! -e "$target" ] && [ ! -L "$target" ]; then
        printf 'no such file or directory\n'
        return
    fi

    if [ -L "$target" ]; then
        kind="symlink -> $(readlink -- "$target")"
    elif [ -d "$target" ]; then
        kind='directory'
    elif [ -f "$target" ]; then
        kind='regular file'
    else
        kind='special file'
    fi

    mode=$(ls -ld -- "$target" | awk '{print $1}')
    printf '%s, mode %s\n' "$kind" "$mode"
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local path full verdict
    path=$1
    full=$(resolve_path "$path")
    verdict=$(check_executable "$path")

    printf '%s\n' "$verdict"
    printf '%s: %s\n' "$full" "$(describe_path "$path")" >&2

    [ "$verdict" = 'Executable' ]
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Create a script that takes an arbitrary number of integer arguments. It should find and print the smallest number among them.

Input: Multiple integer arguments.
Output: The smallest integer.

Example 1: `bash script.sh 5 2 8 1 9`
Example 2: `bash script.sh 100 50 75`
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Print the smallest of the integers given as arguments, or of the
# whitespace-separated integers read on stdin when no argument is given.

set -u

ARGS=()
PROG=

main() {
    PROG=$(script_name)
    ARGS=("$@")
    if (($# == 0)) && ! [[ -t 0 ]]; then
        ARGS=($(stdin_tokens))
    fi
    if ((${#ARGS[@]} == 0)); then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local bad
    bad=$(bad_tokens)
    if [[ -n $bad ]]; then
        fail "not an integer: $bad"
        return 1
    fi

    local raw min
    raw=$(arg_lines | sort -n | head -n 1)
    min=$(normalize $raw)
    printf '%s\n' "$min"
}

script_name() {
    basename -- "$0"
}

usage() {
    printf 'usage: %s INTEGER [INTEGER ...]\n' "$PROG" >&2
}

fail() {
    printf '%s: %s\n' "$PROG" "$1" >&2
}

is_integer() {
    [[ $1 =~ ^[+-]?[0-9]+$ ]]
}

# One token per line, so that stray spaces, tabs or newlines all work.
stdin_tokens() {
    tr -s '[:space:]' '\n'
}

# Comma separated list of the collected tokens that are not integers.
bad_tokens() {
    local arg
    local -a bad=()
    for arg in "${ARGS[@]}"; do
        is_integer "$arg" || bad+=("$arg")
    done
    local IFS=,
    printf '%s' "${bad[*]}"
}

arg_lines() {
    printf '%s\n' "${ARGS[@]}"
}

# Turn "+07" or "-0009" into a plain decimal integer, forcing base 10 so
# that leading zeros are never read as octal.
normalize() {
    local n=${1#+} value
    value=$((10#${n#-}))
    [[ $n == -* ]] && value=$((-value))
    printf '%s\n' "$value"
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Write a script that takes an arbitrary number of arguments. It should print all provided arguments in reverse order, each on a new line.

Input: Multiple arguments.
Output: Arguments in reverse order.

Example 1: `bash script.sh apple banana cherry`
Example 2: `bash script.sh 1 2 3 4 5`
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Print all command line arguments in reverse order, one per line.
set -uo pipefail

progname=$(basename "$0")

print_usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [-n] [-s SEP] ARG...\n' "$progname" >&2
    printf '  -n      number the reversed arguments\n' >&2
    printf '  -s SEP  join the reversed arguments with SEP on one line\n' >&2
}

# Emit the arguments, last one first, one per line.
reverse_args() {
    local i
    for ((i = $#; i > 0; i--)); do
        printf '%s\n' "${!i}"
    done
}

# Collapse the arguments into a single space separated line.
join_args() {
    local IFS=' '
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
}

# Short report on stderr so it never pollutes the reversed listing.
summarize() {
    local original flipped
    original=$(join_args "$@")
    flipped=$(reverse_args "$@" | tr '\n' ' ')
    printf 'processed %d argument(s): %s -> %s\n' "$#" "$original" "${flipped% }" >&2
}

# Prefix each line read from stdin with its index, padded to fit $1 items.
number_lines() {
    local width=${#1} n=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        n=$((n + 1))
        printf '%*d: %s\n' "$width" "$n" "$line"
    done
}

# Write the reversed arguments in the requested layout.
format_output() {
    local separator=$1 numbered=$2 reversed joined
    shift 2
    reversed=$(reverse_args "$@")
    if [[ -n $separator ]]; then
        joined=$(tr '\n' "$separator" <<<"$reversed")
        printf '%s\n' "${joined%"$separator"}"
    elif ((numbered)); then
        number_lines "$#" <<<"$reversed"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$reversed"
    fi
}

main() {
    local numbered=0 separator='' opt
    while getopts ':ns:' opt; do
        case $opt in
            n) numbered=1 ;;
            s) separator=$OPTARG ;;
            *) printf 'unknown option: -%s\n' "$OPTARG" >&2
               print_usage
               return 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    shift $((OPTIND - 1))

    if (($# == 0)); then
        printf '%s: no arguments given\n' "$progname" >&2
        print_usage
        return 1
    fi

    format_output "$separator" "$numbered" "$@"
    summarize "$@"
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Develop a script that takes a directory path as an argument. It should list all hidden files (files starting with '.') in that directory, one per line.

Input: A directory path.
Output: List of hidden file paths.

Example 1: `bash script.sh /home/user`
Example 2: `bash script.sh /etc`
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# List all hidden entries (names beginning with '.') of a directory.

set -u
shopt -s nullglob

usage() {
    local name
    name=$(basename "$0")
    printf 'usage: %s DIRECTORY\n' "$name" >&2
}

# Absolute, symlink-free form of a directory path.
normalize_dir() {
    local resolved
    resolved=$(cd -- "$1" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$resolved"
}

# Print every hidden entry of the directory, one absolute path per line.
list_hidden() {
    local dir=$1 entry base
    for entry in "$dir"/.*; do
        base=$(basename -- "$entry")
        case $base in
            . | ..) continue ;;
        esac
        printf '%s\n' "$entry"
    done
}

# Number of lines in a listing ('' means no entries at all).
count_lines() {
    local listing=$1
    [ -n "$listing" ] || { printf '0\n'; return; }
    printf '%s\n' "$listing" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local target=$1 dir listing total noun
    if [ ! -d "$target" ]; then
        printf 'error: not a directory: %s\n' "$target" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [ ! -r "$target" ] || [ ! -x "$target" ]; then
        printf 'error: cannot read directory: %s\n' "$target" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    dir=$(normalize_dir "$target") || {
        printf 'error: cannot resolve: %s\n' "$target" >&2
        return 1
    }

    listing=$(list_hidden "$dir")
    [ -n "$listing" ] && printf '%s\n' "$listing"

    total=$(count_lines "$listing")
    noun=$([ "$total" -eq 1 ] && printf 'entry' || printf 'entries')
    printf '%s hidden %s in %s\n' "$total" "$noun" "$dir" >&2
    return 0
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Develop a script that takes a string as an argument. It should perform a basic validation to check if the string resembles an email address format (contains '@' and at least one '.' after '@'). Print 'Valid Email' or 'Invalid Email'.

Input: A string.
Output: A string indicating validity.

Example 1: `bash script.sh user@example.com`
Example 2: `bash script.sh invalid-email`
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Basic email-format validation: needs '@' and at least one '.' after the '@'.

set -u

trim() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//'
}

count_char() {
    local text=$1 char=$2
    printf '%s' "$text" | tr -cd "$char" | wc -c | tr -d ' '
}

local_of() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | cut -d '@' -f 1
}

domain_of() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | cut -d '@' -f 2
}

tld_of() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | awk -F '.' '{ print $NF }'
}

validate_email() {
    local email=$1
    local at_count
    at_count=$(count_char "$email" '@')
    if [ "$at_count" -ne 1 ]; then
        echo "expected exactly one '@' but found $at_count"
        return 1
    fi

    local local_part
    local_part=$(local_of "$email")
    if [ -z "$local_part" ]; then
        echo "nothing before the '@'"
        return 1
    fi

    local domain
    domain=$(domain_of "$email")
    local dot_count
    dot_count=$(count_char "$domain" '.')
    if [ "$dot_count" -lt 1 ]; then
        echo "no '.' after the '@'"
        return 1
    fi

    case $domain in
        .*|*.) echo "domain '$domain' starts or ends with a '.'"; return 1 ;;
    esac

    local tld
    tld=$(tld_of "$domain")
    if [ "${#tld}" -lt 2 ]; then
        echo "top-level domain '$tld' is too short"
        return 1
    fi

    echo "local part '$local_part', domain '$domain', tld '$tld'"
    return 0
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
        echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") <string>" >&2
        exit 2
    fi

    local email report status
    email=$(trim "$1")
    report=$(validate_email "$email")
    status=$?

    if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "Valid Email"
        echo "details: $report" >&2
    else
        echo "Invalid Email"
        echo "reason: $report" >&2
    fi
    return "$status"
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Create a script that takes a file or directory path as an argument. It should extract and print the path to its parent directory.

Input: A file or directory path.
Output: The parent directory path.

Example 1: `bash script.sh /home/user/documents/report.txt`
Example 2: `bash script.sh /usr/local/bin`
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Print the parent directory of a given file or directory path.
#
# Usage: script.sh PATH [PATH...]

set -u

usage() {
    local name
    name=$(basename "$0")
    printf 'Usage: %s PATH [PATH...]\n' "$name" >&2
}

# Strip redundant trailing slashes so that "/usr/local/bin/" behaves
# like "/usr/local/bin".
trim_slashes() {
    local path=$1
    while [[ $path == */ && ${#path} -gt 1 ]]; do
        path=${path%/}
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$path"
}

# Pure textual parent, based on the path string only.
parent_of() {
    local path
    path=$(trim_slashes "$1")
    dirname -- "$path"
}

# Absolute parent, resolved against the filesystem when the entry exists.
absolute_parent_of() {
    local parent
    parent=$(parent_of "$1")
    if [[ -d $parent ]]; then
        ( cd -- "$parent" && pwd -P )
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$parent"
    fi
}

report() {
    local target=$1 parent absolute
    parent=$(parent_of "$target")
    printf '%s\n' "$parent"
    absolute=$(absolute_parent_of "$target")
    if [[ $absolute != "$parent" ]]; then
        printf '  (absolute: %s)\n' "$absolute" >&2
    fi
}

main() {
    if (( $# == 0 )); then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local status=0 arg
    for arg in "$@"; do
        if [[ -z $arg ]]; then
            printf 'error: empty path argument\n' >&2
            status=1
            continue
        fi
        if [[ ! -e $arg ]]; then
            printf 'warning: %s does not exist\n' "$arg" >&2
        fi
        report "$arg"
    done
    return "$status"
}

main "$@"

Create a script that takes a string as an argument. It should calculate and print the length of the string, excluding any spaces.

Input: A string.
Output: An integer length.

Example 1: `bash script.sh "hello world"`
Example 2: `bash script.sh "Bash Scripting Fun"`
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Count the characters of a string, ignoring every space it contains.
#
# Usage: bash script.sh [-v] "some string"

set -o nounset
set -o pipefail

PROGNAME=$(basename "$0")

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [-v] "string"\n' "$PROGNAME" >&2
}

# Remove every space character from the argument and echo the result.
strip_spaces() {
    local text=$1
    printf '%s' "${text// /}"
}

# Length of the string once its spaces are gone.
count_nonspace() {
    local text=$1
    local squeezed
    squeezed=$(strip_spaces "$text")
    printf '%s' "${#squeezed}"
}

# How many spaces were dropped, for the verbose report.
count_spaces() {
    local text=$1
    local kept
    kept=$(count_nonspace "$text")
    printf '%s' "$(( ${#text} - kept ))"
}

# Human readable summary used when -v is given.
format_report() {
    local text=$1
    local spaces kept
    spaces=$(count_spaces "$text")
    kept=$(count_nonspace "$text")
    printf '%d character(s), %d space(s) ignored, %d counted' \
        "${#text}" "$spaces" "$kept"
}

main() {
    local verbose=0

    if [[ ${1:-} == -v || ${1:-} == --verbose ]]; then
        verbose=1
        shift
    fi

    if (( $# != 1 )); then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    if (( verbose )); then
        format_report "$1"
        printf '\n'
    else
        count_nonspace "$1"
        printf '\n'
    fi
}

main "$@"

# Human readable summary used when -v is given.
format_report() {
    local text=$1
    local spaces kept
    spaces=`count_spaces "$text"`
    kept=`count_nonspace "$text"`
    printf '%d character(s), %d space(s) ignored, %d counted' \
        "${#text}" "$spaces" "$kept"
}

main() {
    local verbose=0

    if [[ ${1:-} == -v || ${1:-} == --verbose ]]; then
        verbose=1
        shift
    fi

    if (( $# != 1 )); then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    if (( verbose )); then
        format_report "$1"
        printf '\n'
    else
        count_nonspace "$1"
        printf '\n'
    fi
}

A single Base64 encoded string argument.

The decoded string.

./decode.sh "SGVsbG8gV29ybGQ="
Expected Output: Hello World

./decode.sh "YmFzaCBzY3JpcHRpbmc="
Expected Output: bash scripting

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# decode.sh - decode a Base64 encoded string given on the command line.

set -u

readonly PROGRAM_NAME="$(basename "$0")"

usage() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $PROGRAM_NAME <base64-string>

Decodes the given Base64 encoded string and prints the result.
EOF
}

# Locate a usable base64 decoder and report the flag needed to decode.
decoder_command() {
    if command -v base64 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "base64 -d"
    elif command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "openssl base64 -d"
    else
        return 1
    fi
}

# Strip whitespace and newlines that often sneak into copied Base64 blobs.
normalize() {
    local raw="$1"
    printf '%s' "$(tr -d '[:space:]' <<<"$raw")"
}

# A valid Base64 payload uses the standard alphabet, has a length that is a
# multiple of four and carries at most two padding characters at the end.
is_valid_base64() {
    local data="$1"
    local length="${#data}"

    if (( length == 0 || length % 4 != 0 )); then
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! $data =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$ ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

decode_base64() {
    local data
    data="$(normalize "$1")"

    if ! is_valid_base64 "$data"; then
        echo "$PROGRAM_NAME: not a valid Base64 string: $1" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    local decoder
    if ! decoder="$(decoder_command)"; then
        echo "$PROGRAM_NAME: no base64 or openssl utility available" >&2
        return 3
    fi

    local decoded
    if ! decoded="$(printf '%s' "$data" | $decoder 2>/dev/null)"; then
        echo "$PROGRAM_NAME: failed to decode input" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    printf '%s\n' "$decoded"
}

main() {
    if (( $# != 1 )) || [[ $1 == -h || $1 == --help ]]; then
        usage >&2
        return 1
    fi

    decode_base64 "$1"
}

main "$@"

topic: Print File Size in Human Readable Format
text_es:
Write a script that takes a filename as a command-line argument and prints its size in human-readable format (e.g., 1K, 234M, 2G).

Input:
A single filename argument.

Output:
The file size in human-readable format.

Example Invocations:
./filesize.sh /etc/hosts
Expected Output: (e.g., 12K)

./filesize.sh /bin/bash
Expected Output: (e.g., 1.1M)
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# filesize.sh -- print the size of a file in human-readable form (1K, 234M, 2G).

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
    local prog
    prog=$(basename "$0")
    printf 'usage: %s FILE\n' "$prog" >&2
}

# Print the size of "$1" in bytes, using whichever stat(1) flavour is present.
file_bytes() {
    local path=$1 size
    if size=$(stat -c %s -- "$path" 2>/dev/null); then
        printf '%s' "$size"
    else
        size=$(stat -f %z -- "$path")
        printf '%s' "$size"
    fi
}

# Print how many times the byte count must be divided by 1024 to stay under 1024.
unit_index() {
    local bytes=$1 idx=0
    while (( bytes >= 1024 && idx < 6 )); do
        bytes=$(( bytes / 1024 ))
        idx=$(( idx + 1 ))
    done
    printf '%s' "$idx"
}

# Scale a byte count and attach its unit suffix, keeping one decimal for
# small mantissas the way du -h does.
human_readable() {
    local bytes=$1
    local units=(B K M G T P E)
    local idx scaled
    idx=$(unit_index "$bytes")
    scaled=$(awk -v b="$bytes" -v p="$idx" 'BEGIN {
        v = b / (1024 ^ p)
        if (p > 0 && v < 10) printf "%.1f", v
        else printf "%.0f", v
    }')
    printf '%s%s' "$scaled" "${units[idx]}"
}

main() {
    if (( $# != 1 )); then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local path=$1
    if [[ -d $path ]]; then
        printf '%s: is a directory\n' "$path" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -f $path || ! -r $path ]]; then
        printf '%s: not a readable file\n' "$path" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local bytes pretty
    bytes=$(file_bytes "$path")
    pretty=$(human_readable "$bytes")
    printf '%s\n' "$pretty"
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Write a script that counts and prints the total number of regular files in the current working directory.

Input:
None.

Output:
The total count of regular files.

Example Invocations:
./count_current_files.sh
(If current directory has 3 regular files)
Expected Output: 3

./count_current_files.sh
(If current directory has 0 regular files)
Expected Output: 0
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# count_current_files.sh - report how many regular files live in the
# current working directory (non-recursive).

set -u

# Count the regular files directly inside the given directory.
count_regular_files() {
    local dir="$1"
    local marks
    marks=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf 'x' | wc -c)
    printf '%s\n' "$marks"
}

# Count the sub-directories of the given directory.
count_subdirectories() {
    local dir="$1"
    local marks
    marks=$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -printf 'x' | wc -c)
    printf '%s\n' "$marks"
}

# Total bytes occupied by the regular files of the directory.
total_file_size() {
    local dir="$1"
    local bytes
    bytes=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%s\n' | awk '{ s += $1 } END { print s + 0 }')
    printf '%s\n' "$bytes"
}

# Print a human readable summary of the directory contents.
print_report() {
    local dir="$1"
    local files dirs bytes
    files=$(count_regular_files "$dir")
    dirs=$(count_subdirectories "$dir")
    bytes=$(total_file_size "$dir")
    printf 'Directory : %s\n' "$dir"
    printf 'Files     : %s\n' "$files"
    printf 'Dirs      : %s\n' "$dirs"
    printf 'Bytes     : %s\n' "$bytes"
}

usage() {
    local name
    name=$(basename "$0")
    printf 'Usage: %s [-v]\n' "$name" >&2
    printf '  -v   print a verbose report instead of the bare count\n' >&2
}

main() {
    local verbose=0 opt
    while getopts ':vh' opt; do
        case "$opt" in
            v) verbose=1 ;;
            h) usage; return 0 ;;
            *) usage; return 2 ;;
        esac
    done

    local dir
    dir=$(pwd)

    if [ ! -r "$dir" ]; then
        printf 'error: cannot read %s\n' "$dir" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    if [ "$verbose" -eq 1 ]; then
        print_report "$dir"
    else
        count_regular_files "$dir"
    fi
}

main "$@"

text_es:
Write a script that prints the primary group name of the current user.

Input:
None.

Output:
The primary group name.

Example Invocations:
./primary_group.sh
Expected Output: (e.g., 'users')

./primary_group.sh
Expected Output: (e.g., 'staff')
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# primary_group.sh - print the primary group name of the current user.
#
# The name is resolved in three steps: find the numeric primary GID of the
# running user, translate that GID into a name using the name service, and
# fall back to /etc/group if getent is unavailable.

set -u

current_user() {
    local name
    name=$(id -un 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ -z $name ]]; then
        name=${USER:-${LOGNAME:-}}
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$name"
}

primary_gid() {
    local gid
    gid=$(id -g 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ ! $gid =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$gid"
}

gid_from_group_file() {
    local gid=$1
    awk -F: -v want="$gid" '$3 == want { print $1; exit }' /etc/group
}

gid_to_name() {
    local gid=$1 name=""

    if command -v getent >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        name=$(getent group "$gid" | cut -d: -f1)
    fi

    if [[ -z $name && -r /etc/group ]]; then
        name=$(gid_from_group_file "$gid")
    fi

    [[ -n $name ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$name"
}

primary_group() {
    local gid name

    # id -gn does the whole job on most systems; prefer it when it works.
    name=$(id -gn 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ -n $name ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$name"
        return 0
    fi

    gid=$(primary_gid) || return 1
    gid_to_name "$gid"
}

main() {
    local group
    if ! group=$(primary_group); then
        printf 'primary_group.sh: cannot determine primary group for %s\n' \
            "$(current_user)" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$group"
}

main "$@"

topic: Print Every Nth Line of a File
text_es:
Write a script that takes a filename and an integer N as arguments. It should print every Nth line of the file.

Input:
A filename and an integer N.

Example Invocations:
./every_nth.sh data.txt 2
(Assume data.txt: '1\n2\n3\n4\n5')
Expected Output: 2\n4

./every_nth.sh list.txt 3

Write a script that takes a string and a character as arguments. It should print the string with all occurrences of the specified character removed.

Input:
A string and a single character.

Output:
The modified string.

Example Invocations:
./remove_char.sh "hello world" "l"
Expected Output: heo word

./remove_char.sh "banana" "a"
Expected Output: bnn
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# remove_char.sh - print a string with every occurrence of a character removed.

set -u

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [-v] <string> <char>\n' "$(basename "$0")" >&2
}

# Succeeds only for a single-character argument.
validate_char() {
    local c=$1
    if [ ${#c} -ne 1 ]; then
        printf '%s: the second argument must be exactly one character\n' \
            "$(basename "$0")" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

# Strip every occurrence of $2 from $1 and print the result.
remove_char() {
    local subject=$1 target=$2
    printf '%s' "${subject//"$target"/}"
}

# How many characters the removal actually took out.
count_removed() {
    local subject=$1 target=$2
    local stripped
    stripped=$(remove_char "$subject" "$target")
    printf '%s' $(( ${#subject} - ${#stripped} ))
}

# Human readable name of a character, for the verbose report.
describe_char() {
    local c=$1
    case $c in
        ' ')  printf 'a space' ;;
        "$(printf '\t')") printf 'a tab' ;;
        *)    printf "'%s'" "$c" ;;
    esac
}

main() {
    local verbose=0
    while [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ "$1" = "-v" ]; do
        verbose=1
        shift
    done

    if [ $# -ne 2 ]; then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local subject=$1 target=$2
    validate_char "$target" || return 2

    local result
    result=$(remove_char "$subject" "$target")
    printf '%s\n' "$result"

    if [ "$verbose" -eq 1 ]; then
        printf 'removed %s occurrence(s) of %s; %d characters remain\n' \
            "$(count_removed "$subject" "$target")" \
            "$(describe_char "$target")" \
            "${#result}" >&2
    fi
}

main "$@"

topic: List Files by Modification Time (Newest First)
text_es:
Write a script that takes a directory path as an argument and lists all regular files in it, sorted by modification time (newest first).

Input:
A single directory path argument.

Output:
A list of filenames, one per line, sorted by modification time.

Example Invocations:
./list_by_mtime.sh .
Expected Output: (e.g., 'newest_file.txt\nolder_file.txt')

./list_by_mtime.sh /var/log
Expected Output: (e.g., 'syslog\nauth.log')
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# list_by_mtime.sh -- list the regular files of a directory, newest first.

set -u

prog=$(basename -- "$0")
kernel=$(uname -s)

# GNU stat and BSD stat disagree on how to ask for the modification time.
case $kernel in
    Darwin | *BSD) stat_mtime=(stat -f '%m' --) ;;
    *)             stat_mtime=(stat -c '%Y' --) ;;
esac

usage() {
    printf 'usage: %s DIRECTORY\n' "$prog" >&2
}

validate_dir() {
    local dir=$1
    if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then

Input:
A search string followed by one or more filenames.

Output:
Filenames containing the search string, one per line.

Example Invocations:
./find_in_files.sh "error" log1.txt log2.txt
(Assume log1.txt has 'error', log2.txt doesn't)
Expected Output: log1.txt

./find_in_files.sh "bash" script1.sh script2.sh
(Assume both have 'bash')
Expected Output: script1.sh\nscript2.sh
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# find_in_files.sh - print the names of the files that contain a search string.
# Usage: ./find_in_files.sh [-n] PATTERN FILE [FILE...]
set -u
progname=$(basename "$0")
show_lines=0

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [-n] PATTERN FILE [FILE...]\n' "$progname" >&2
}

# Number of lines in FILE that hold PATTERN as literal text.
count_matches() {
    local pattern=$1 file=$2 hits
    hits=$(grep -c -F -e "$pattern" -- "$file")
    printf '%s' "$hits"
}

file_contains() {
    local hits
    hits=$(count_matches "$1" "$2")
    [ "$hits" -gt 0 ]
}

first_match_line() {
    local pattern=$1 file=$2 located
    located=$(grep -n -m1 -F -e "$pattern" -- "$file")
    printf '%s' "${located%%:*}"
}

report_match() {
    local pattern=$1 file=$2 lineno
    if [ "$show_lines" -eq 1 ]; then
        lineno=$(first_match_line "$pattern" "$file")
        printf '%s:%s\n' "$file" "$lineno"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$file"
    fi
}

validate_file() {
    local file=$1
    if [ -f "$file" ] && [ -r "$file" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    printf '%s: %s: not a readable file\n' "$progname" "$file" >&2
    return 1
}

main() {
    local opt
    while getopts ':n' opt; do
        case $opt in
            n) show_lines=1 ;;
            *) usage; return 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    shift $((OPTIND - 1))
    if [ "$#" -lt 2 ]; then
        usage
        return 2
    fi
    local pattern=$1 file status=1 skipped=0
    shift
    for file in "$@"; do
        if ! validate_file "$file"; then
            skipped=1
            continue
        fi
        if file_contains "$pattern" "$file"; then
            report_match "$pattern" "$file"
            status=0
        fi
    done
    if [ "$status" -ne 0 ] && [ "$skipped" -ne 0 ]; then
        return 2
    fi
    return "$status"
}

main "$@"

Write a script that prints the kernel version of the operating system.

Input:
None.

Output:
The kernel version string.

Example Invocations:
./kernel_version.sh
Expected Output: (e.g., 'Linux 5.15.0-86-generic')

./kernel_version.sh
Expected Output: (e.g., 'Linux 6.2.0-34-generic')
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# kernel_version.sh - print the kernel version of the operating system.

set -u

# Name of the running kernel (e.g. "Linux", "Darwin").
kernel_name() {
    uname -s
}

# Release string of the running kernel (e.g. "5.15.0-86-generic").
kernel_release() {
    uname -r
}

# Numeric part of the release, useful for comparisons and reporting.
kernel_base_version() {
    local release
    release=$(kernel_release)
    printf '%s\n' "${release%%-*}"
}

# "<name> <release>", the string the task asks for.
kernel_version() {
    local name release
    name=$(kernel_name)
    release=$(kernel_release)
    printf '%s %s\n' "$name" "$release"
}

# Split the base version into its major/minor components.
kernel_major() {
    local base
    base=$(kernel_base_version)
    printf '%s\n' "${base%%.*}"
}

kernel_minor() {
    local base rest
    base=$(kernel_base_version)
    rest=${base#*.}
    printf '%s\n' "${rest%%.*}"
}

# uname must be available and must actually answer, otherwise we cannot report.
check_uname() {
    local release
    if ! command -v uname >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "kernel_version.sh: uname not found" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    release=$(kernel_release)
    if [ -z "$release" ]; then
        echo "kernel_version.sh: kernel release is empty" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

# Extra line describing the kernel in a human friendly way.
kernel_report() {
    local name major minor release
    name=$(kernel_name)
    major=$(kernel_major)
    minor=$(kernel_minor)
    release=$(kernel_release)
    printf '%s kernel %s.%s (release %s)\n' "$name" "$major" "$minor" "$release"
}

main() {
    check_uname || return 1

    kernel_version

    if [ "${1:-}" = "--verbose" ]; then
        kernel_report
    fi
}

main "$@"

topic: Check if a String Starts With a Prefix
text_es:
Write a script that takes a string and a prefix as arguments. It should print 'Starts with prefix' if the string starts with the given prefix, otherwise 'Does not start with prefix'.

Input:
A string and a prefix string.

Output:
A status message.

Example Invocations:
./starts_with.sh "hello world" "hello"
Expected Output: Starts with prefix

./starts_with.sh "bash script" "script"
Expected Output: Does not start with prefix
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# starts_with.sh — report whether a string begins with a given prefix.
#
# Usage: starts_with.sh [-i] <string> <prefix>
#
# Exit status: 0 when the string starts with the prefix, 1 when it does not,
# 2 when the arguments are wrong.

set -u

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [-i] <string> <prefix>\n' "$(basename "$0")" >&2
}

main() {
    local fold=no opt verdict

    while getopts ':i' opt; do
        case $opt in
            i) fold=yes ;;
            *) usage; return 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    shift $((OPTIND - 1))

    if (( $# != 2 )); then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    verdict=$(describe_match "$1" "$2" "$fold")
    printf '%s\n' "$verdict"

    [[ $verdict == 'Starts with prefix' ]]
}

# Human readable verdict for one string/prefix pair.
describe_match() {
    if starts_with "$1" "$2" "$3"; then
        printf 'Starts with prefix'
    else
        printf 'Does not start with prefix'
    fi
}

# Exit status 0 when "$1" begins with "$2"; "$3" is "yes" to ignore case.
starts_with() {
    local text=$1 prefix=$2 fold=$3

    if [[ $fold == yes ]]; then
        text=$(to_lower "$text")
        prefix=$(to_lower "$prefix")
    fi

    if (( ${#prefix} > ${#text} )); then
        return 1
    fi

    [[ $(first_chars "$text" "${#prefix}") == "$prefix" ]]
}

to_lower() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'
}

# Echo the first "$2" characters of "$1".
first_chars() {
    local text=$1 count=$2
    printf '%s' "${text:0:count}"
}

main "$@"

Write a script that takes a string as a command-line argument and prints it with leading whitespace removed.

Input:
A single string argument.

Output:
The string with leading whitespace trimmed.

Example Invocations:
./trim_leading.sh "   Hello World"
Expected Output: Hello World

./trim_leading.sh "  Bash Script"
Expected Output: Bash Script
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# trim_leading.sh -- print a string with its leading whitespace removed.

set -u

usage() {
    printf 'Usage: %s [-v] STRING\n' "$(basename "$0")" >&2
    printf '  -v  also report the whitespace that was stripped (on stderr)\n' >&2
}

# Remove every leading whitespace character (space, tab, CR, ...) from $1.
trim_leading() {
    local s=$1
    printf '%s' "$s" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//'
}

# Echo just the whitespace prefix that trim_leading would discard.
leading_prefix() {
    local s=$1 body
    body=$(trim_leading "$s")
    printf '%s' "${s%"$body"}"
}

# Count how many times character $2 occurs in string $1.
count_char() {
    local s=$1 stripped
    stripped=$(printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d "$2")
    printf '%s' $(( ${#s} - ${#stripped} ))
}

# Human readable summary of the stripped prefix.
describe_prefix() {
    local prefix=$1 spaces tabs others
    spaces=$(count_char "$prefix" ' ')
    tabs=$(count_char "$prefix" '\t')
    others=$(( ${#prefix} - spaces - tabs ))
    printf 'stripped %d char(s): %d space, %d tab, %d other' \
        "${#prefix}" "$spaces" "$tabs" "$others"
}

main() {
    local verbose=0
    while [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ "$1" = "-v" ]; do
        verbose=1
        shift
    done

    if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
        usage
        return 2
    fi

    local trimmed
    trimmed=$(trim_leading "$1")
    printf '%s\n' "$trimmed"

    if [ "$verbose" -eq 1 ]; then
        local prefix
        prefix=$(leading_prefix "$1")
        printf '%s\n' "$(describe_prefix "$prefix")" >&2
    fi
}

main "$@"
